sources.title: Site Layer 1, LLC: Initial NSR air-quality construction permit application for the Site Layer 1 Data Center Project, Grant County, New Mexico (cover letter 7 October 2026; posted by NMED Air Quality Bureau)
sources.publisher: Site Layer 1, LLC (applicant), prepared by SWCA Environmental Consultants; published by the New Mexico Environment Department
sources.source_family: NMED Air Quality Bureau permit applications
sources.attribution: Site Layer 1, LLC; New Mexico Environment Department Air Quality Bureau
sources.summary: The 191-page application, under a cover letter of 7 October 2026 submitting 'this initial NSR application for the Site Layer 1 facility proposed in Grant and Hidalgo Counties', is titled 'Site Layer 1 Data Center Project, Grant County, New Mexico, Initial NSR Application, October 2026'. Its Application Summary states that 'Site Layer 1, LLC (Site Layer 1) is proposing to construct a data center powered by a natural gas–fired electrical power generation development (the “Project”), on private land in Hidalgo and Grant Counties', that 'The anticipated data center size is approximately 800 megawatts (MW), with on-site gas generation providing approximately 300 MW', and that the generation project area is 7,214.4 acres wholly in the Grant County parcel; the plant is 32 Wärtsilä 20V34SG gas engines of about 9.4 MW each with SCR and oxidation catalysts (SIC 4911). Section 1 lists Site Layer 1, LLC as plant owner and operator, status 'Not Constructed', anticipated construction start Q1 2027, completion Q3 2028 and start-up Q4 2028, and gives the facility location as latitude 31.980569, longitude -108.511384 (UTM zone 12, NAD 83: 735,145 E, 3,540,987 N; County Grant; elevation 4,540 ft; 4.9 miles north-east of Playas; land status Private). The modeling report says the Project 'consists of a natural gas–fired electrical generation and data center development' and its preliminary layout (Figure 2, 'Data Center & Gas Engine Site Plan') draws four data-centre buildings beside the engine hall. The public-notice letters to counties of 27 August 2026 announce the application 'for the construction of its data center powered by natural-gas fired electrical power generation facility' at 31.980165 N, 108.511324 W.
sources.date_semantics: Cover letter dated 7 October 2026 (PDF created 6 October and modified 7 October 2026; form pages printed 6 October 2026); NMED lists the document as the 'Initial Construction Permit Application' for 'Site Layer I, LLC – Site Layer I data center' under Grant County on its public-notices page (us-co-wy-mt-nm-p5-nmed-public-notices-page, captured 27 October 2026). published_at is the cover-letter date, used as the announcement observation; no permit has been issued and no construction stage is asserted. Construction and start-up dates and the 800 MW and 300 MW figures are applicant targets, not observations or measured IT load.

sources.title: City of Prineville City Council meeting of 13 October 2026: agenda packet, including Resolution No. 1654 and the development agreement with Apple, Inc. for the PRZ-06 Offsite Utility Expansion Project
sources.pages_reviewed: packet pages 22-37 (item 7: staff report, Resolution No. 1654, development agreement with recitals, Exhibit B cost schedule, Exhibit A Parametrix plan and the pipeline map), read with pdftotext and rendered with pdftoppm
sources.summary: The Public Works staff report for item 7 asks the council to approve Resolution 1654 so that the City can enter a development agreement with Apple, Inc. for administrative oversight of the 'PRZ-06 Offsite Utility Expansion Project', which coordinates 'the construction of utility improvements necessary to serve Apple's eastern campus expansion'. Its background states that 'Apple's initial development plan included the expansion of the easter[n] portion of its campus', which 'requires offsite utility improvements to serve the development of this area' (16-inch domestic water, 12-inch non-potable water, 21-inch sanitary sewer, 12-inch reclaimed/industrial wastewater, 8-inch gravity and 4-inch pressure sewer lines, bored under Highway 126 in 54-inch and 24-inch steel casings). Recital A of the attached agreement states that Apple 'owns and operates a data center campus on real property located within City, as described in Exhibit A', and recital B that the project is the offsite utility infrastructure 'needed to serve the eastern portion the User's campus PRZ 06 development area within Prineville, Oregon'. Exhibit A (Parametrix, 'System Improvements at Points of Connection') labels the APPLE CAMPUS and shows the PRZ06 offsite lines reaching its north side and running along its eastern edge, with pressure tables for campus phases 1B, 2B and buildout. Apple reimburses the City's costs up to USD 8,803,435.44 plus an 8.5 percent administrative fee; the City is to strive for Final Completion of the utility project by 31 March 2028 and to reserve 350 gpm of future water delivery (in addition to 99 gpm current delivery) until Apple calls for it or 30 September 2028. This dated government record names Apple's eastern campus expansion in the PRZ 06 development area of the existing Prineville campus as a planned development; it does not describe the buildings, floor area, power or IT capacity, permits or construction start of the expansion, and the utility schedule and water reservation are forecasts, not observations.
sources.date_semantics: published_at is the creation time of the AgendaCenter packet PDF (2026-10-08T17:29:07Z per its PDF metadata; the AgendaCenter index shows no posting time). The announcement is taken as observed on the packet date, 8 October 2026; the council adopted the resolution on 13 October 2026 (us-or-wa-p5-prineville-cc-20261027-packet). This is the same capture already published as evidence for the campus's existing-operations project (retrieved 22 October 2026 by lane us-west-mountain-p1; metadata reproduced exactly so that the existing evidence row is reused). A recheck capture on 27 October 2026 (recheck_capture_file, 03:23:11Z) returned byte-identical content (same SHA-256).
